newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng drops sharply in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng drops sharply in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 161 points to 13,448 at the open, prompted by Wall Street's drop and renewed interest rate jitters.
The Hang Seng Index eased further, declining 204 points to 13,405 in early trade. Turnover was a moderately heavy HK$1.02 billion.

"The drop is in line with the fall on Wall Street," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities, adding that it was a fall in sympathy with the U.S. market and not one based on fundamentals.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slumped 94.28 points to 6,755.75 on Thursday due to programme selling in the S&P 500 futures market which later prompted sell programmes on other markets.
"We are recommending a buy on weakness for Hong Kong," said Lai.
Commercial and industrial sector issues took the brunt of the early sell-off. Properties and utilities also were flooded with sell orders.
Blue chip conglomerate Hutchison Whampoa, as well as parent Cheung Kong, were especially hard hit after their strong run-up following the announcement of the group restructuring.
Hutchison Whampoa was the most actively traded issue on trade of HK$370.19 million, falling HK$1.75 to HK$62.25. Cheung Kong shed HK$1.00 to HK$73.75.
"These are good prices to accumulate these counters," said Boby Ho, dealing director at G.K. Goh Securities.
Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.25 to HK$90.00 and Great Eagle dropped HK$0.80 to HK$34.10.
Hongkong Telecom slumped HK$0.25 to HK$13.00 on moderate volume of HK$88.92 million.

Profit-taking in HSBC Holdings brought the bank down HK$2.50 to HK$177.50 on heavy volume of HK$430.95 million. The share gained HK$15.00 last week, chiefly on derivative-induced buying interest, brokers said.
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures at the open pushed the January contract down to a low of 13,200. After 50 minutes of trade, the contract was trading 230 points lower at 13,355.
